topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture's scope and learning objectives regarding cancer therapies and their modes of action.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss conventional non-targeted treatment modalities—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—and their associated mechanisms and systemic toxicities.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: They examine targeted therapeutic strategies designed to exploit specific biological vulnerabilities and checkpoint or repair defects within cancer cells.

topics.label: Targeting oncogene addiction and kinase inhibitor resistance
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the principles of targeting hyperactivated kinases with small-molecule inhibitors along with the biological mechanisms underlying resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the use of monoclonal antibodies and targeted antibody conjugates to selectively deliver cytotoxic effects to cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: They cover the mechanisms and clinical applications of cancer immunotherapy, ranging from checkpoint blockade to engineered T-cell and bispecific therapies.

topics.label: Global challenges, trends, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate broader clinical challenges, historical survival trends, and future strategic and ethical considerations in cancer therapy.
